content.title: About
content.content: Ruffled plain potato chips are thinly sliced potatoes fried until crisp. They have a light salty taste and a characteristic wavy surface that holds dips and adds extra crunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ruffled chips were introduced in the United States in the 1950s to increase surface area and improve dip retention.
A special corrugated cutter creates the wavy texture during slicing.
Starchy potatoes are chosen for their ability to become extra crunchy when fried.
In some countries they are colloquially called “potato waffles” because of their shape.
Plain ruffled chips are suitable for people who limit added flavors and salt.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Potato chips provide carbohydrates that quickly supply energy.

items.title: Potassium content
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C presence
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C survives rapid frying, offering antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: Unlike sweet snacks, plain ruffled chips contain virtually no sugar.

items.title: Easy digestibility
items.content: Thin slices cook quickly, making them easy to digest.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Chips are fried, so they are high in calories and fat.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Even plain chips often contain a modest amount of salt added during frying.

items.title: Aflatoxins
items.content: Improper storage of potatoes can lead to mold that produces aflatoxins.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes or to the frying oils used.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy chips as a snack on their own, with dips such as salsa, guacamole, or cheese sauce, or sprinkle them over salads for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from light. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to prevent oil oxidation.
